name: time-field
pattern: A headless time field adding cancelable change events and state outputs to native input[type=time]
responsibility: Preserves native time value, min, max, step, segment editing, picker UI, and form semantics. Adds user-originated change events, data-state, and semantic markup validation that native input lacks. Does not generate appearance or content.

authorMarkup.label: The consumer provides an accessible name through <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby.
authorMarkup.range: The consumer supplies min, max, step, and value as native attributes.
authorMarkup.form: The consumer supplies name and uses native time-input form submission.
authorMarkup.content: The controller does not generate elements or content.

semanticElements: The root must be an HTMLInputElement with type=time.
contractValidation.invalidMarkup: Validate the root on connection. Invalid markup prevents listener registration, state output, and value operations and issues console.warn once per connection. Do not throw.
contractValidation.warning: Use the standard English disabling warning, including the required native input[type=time] root.

value.description: Current native input.value. All three engines preserve the assigned form, which may be HH:MM, HH:MM:SS, or HH:MM:SS.sss. Missing or invalid input is an empty string. Assignment changes value and data-state without custom events.

time-field:beforechange.when: Before a value change from trusted pointer or keyboard interaction (native change from segment editing or picker UI)

detail.value: The proposed value (an HH:MM-family string or an empty string)

time-field:beforechange.effect: On preventDefault(), restore the previous native value and data-state and suppress time-field:change.

time-field:change.when: After a trusted value change is committed

events.programmatic: The value setter, initialization, form reset, and reconnection do not emit custom events.
events.sameValue: Do not emit beforechange/change for unchanged values. Compare value strings exactly: different forms of the same time are distinct values because the native input preserves their form.
events.synthetic: input/change with isTrusted=false only synchronize native value and state outputs; they do not emit custom events. The controller does not dispatch synthetic native input/change events.

consumerIntegration.stimulusActions: Listen for time-field:change and time-field:beforechange on the root or an ancestor. The controller does not stop propagation.
consumerIntegration.cancelableHook: Cancel a change by calling event.preventDefault() in a time-field:beforechange listener.
consumerIntegration.programmatic: Other controllers may read/write value through a Stimulus controller reference or outlets. Programmatic API changes emit no events.
consumerIntegration.nested: Use :self or event.target === event.currentTarget to restrict events to the root when listening outside nested time-field controllers.

behavior.scope: Use one native input[type=time] as the root; there are no targets.
behavior.initial: Use the native value attribute as the initial value. The controller has no separate initial value.
behavior.native: Delegate segment navigation, increment/decrement, digit entry, deletion, picker UI, and form semantics to the browser. The controller neither validates nor corrects values.
behavior.disabled: Do not add data-* attributes for disabled state. Public API changes are allowed regardless of disabled state.

keyboard.native: Do not implement keyboard handling. Native segment editing exists in all three engines. Measurements show the hour segment initially active in each engine and ArrowUp advancing through a 24-hour cycle.
keyboard.pageKeys: Do not implement PageUp/PageDown. Firefox handles them per segment (hours advance by three and wrap at 12; minutes advance by ten), while Chromium and WebKit do not respond. See docs/notes/browser-engine-differences.md. Whole-value navigation would duplicate Firefox segment handling and produce inconsistent results. The controller cannot determine segment focus and does not normalize these engine differences.

managedMarkup.nativeSemantics: Use native input[type=time] value, min, max, step, keyboard handling, and form semantics. There is no implicit role, and accessibility-tree exposure is engine-dependent.
managedMarkup.aria: Do not write role or aria-* attributes. Do not overwrite or remove authored ARIA.
managedMarkup.stateOnly: Only root data-state is a controller-managed state output. Do not output CSS custom properties.
managedMarkup.preservation: Preserve authored id, name, value, min, max, step, disabled, ARIA, and other attributes.

stateOutputs.ownership: Only root data-state is controller-owned; do not use ARIA as a visual state output.
stateOutputs.comparison: Compare min/max using valueAsNumber (milliseconds since midnight), not strings. A time value may use HH:MM, HH:MM:SS, or HH:MM:SS.sss while bounds retain their authored strings. min="10:30" and value="10:30:00" represent the same time but differ as strings, incorrectly producing between instead of min; this was measured in all three engines (docs/notes/browser-engine-differences.md). Date-field can compare fixed-width YYYY-MM-DD strings; that reasoning does not apply to time.
stateOutputs.boundResolution: Parse min/max by assigning each string to a detached <input type="time"> created in the root ownerDocument and reading valueAsNumber. Delegate interpretation to the engine rather than parsing HH:MM:SS.sss with custom regular expressions. Empty or invalid strings yield NaN and are excluded as bounds using Number.isNaN.
stateOutputs.min: data-state="min" when valueAsNumber equals min in milliseconds. Missing or invalid min cannot produce this state.
stateOutputs.max: data-state="max" when valueAsNumber equals max in milliseconds. Missing or invalid max cannot produce this state.
stateOutputs.between: data-state="between" otherwise, including empty values whose valueAsNumber is NaN.

lifecycle: Register root keydown, pointerdown, input, and change listeners and the associated-form reset listener in connect(); remove them in disconnect().
The controller instance retains the detached input used to parse min/max; never insert it into the document.
Synchronize state output from the current native value on reconnection.
Do not duplicate listeners or custom events when reconnecting the same instance

observations.environment: Native browser pickers and screen readers on real devices
observations.item: Picker opening/closing, accessibility-tree exposure, and announcements
observations.impact: The controller retains native time input semantics and does not implement the picker or an alternative AT mapping.

acceptanceCriteria: Required AAA criteria: 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception), with no pointer-only features; and 3.2.5 Change on Request, with controller focus movement limited to user actions or consumer JS calls, never timers.
The behavior and accessibility implemented by this component must meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA.
Conforming input[type=time] preserves native value, min, max, step, segment editing, and form semantics. The controller never intercepts keyboard operations.
Determine data-state through valueAsNumber so different forms of the same time, such as min="10:30" and value="10:30:00", produce min.
Only trusted value changes emit one cancelable beforechange followed by one committed change, in that order. Cancellation preserves value and state.
Public API calls, initialization, form reset, and reconnection synchronize state outputs without custom events.
The controller adds neither role nor aria-* attributes and preserves authored attributes.
Invalid markup disables enhancement with one warning
Pass automated tests in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. Tests must not depend on WebKit delaying change until blur; see docs/notes/browser-engine-differences.md.

Arrow-key tests use min/max allowing the hour segment to move. Fixing the hour through bounds makes only Chromium leave both value and events unchanged, for the same reason as date-field's widenRange.
Report picker opening/closing, accessibility-tree exposure, and real-device screen reader announcements as unverified.

testMatrix.description: data-state min/max/between, missing min/max, empty values, and authored-attribute preservation
Equivalent times with different forms, such as min="10:30" and value="10:30:00"; invalid bounds treated as absent; and second-bearing values with step="1"
beforechange cancellation and restoration; change detail, order, and bubbling
Wrapping trusted native change from segment editing and determining its reason
No events from value assignment or synthetic input/change, with state synchronization
One warning and disabled enhancement for invalid roots

testMatrix: No controller handling of PageUp/PageDown (covered by time-field-native-change)
Engine-specific results for Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit
Screen-reader results on a real device (unverified)
